studies.finding: A single evocation produces no significant IL-2 suppression relative to its own control in the reported comparison.
limitations: The main scientific text, Methods and legends of Figures 1-3 plus the displayed captions for Tables S1-S2 were read in PMC HTML. The separate DOCX tables, raw cytokine/flow data and earlier publication behind experiment A were not read or replayed. Experiment A explicitly reuses previously published observations re-expressed relative to baseline; it is not new independent replication. A and B are separate cohorts with different evocation schedules and intervals to the final blood draw. Main prose lists an unusual closely spaced final evening evocation in A; no exact common twelve-hour evocation schedule is inferred.
The measured response is cytokine release by isolated stimulated cells, not direct plasma IL-2, every immune function, infection outcome or transplant benefit.

The placebo-only acquisition control does not match cyclosporine history with an unpaired cue/drug schedule; the protocol contrast does not uniquely isolate association-specific learning from all lasting history effects.
Four versus one evocation is a comparison of separate experiments/cohorts with schedule and sampling differences, not a fully matched randomized dose-response test or proof that four is a minimum.
Drug washout measurements constrain simple persistence but do not identify a complete brain-to-spleen neural route; the paper's proposed anatomy cites other experiments.
